content.overview: Article 36 provides that, unless the context otherwise requires, 'the State' has the same meaning as in Part III. Part IV obligations therefore address the same State entities as Fundamental Rights analysis, subject to context.

sections.heading: Textual function
sections.body: Article 36 is a definition clause for Part IV. It links the Directive Principles to the Part III concept of the State. Verify the exact wording in the official Constitution text.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: When arguing State obligation under a Directive Principle or implementing law, identify which instrumentality of the State is alleged to act — the same analytical habit as under Article 12.
